title: Does the crash-test rating cover the car you are buying?
meta_description: Match a safety rating to an imported car’s market, build date and equipment, using Euro NCAP, ANCAP, IIHS and NHTSA examples.
h1: Does the crash-test rating cover the car you are buying?
summary: A safety badge is useful only within its published coverage. Learn how to distinguish a supported rating claim from a missing equipment record or an unsupported transfer between versions.
body_markdown:
# Does the crash-test rating cover the car you are buying?

A seller sends a five-star graphic with a vehicle quotation. The model name matches, but the image does not identify the market specification, production period or safety equipment. Is that enough to choose the car? No: it establishes a claim to investigate, not that the offered unit is covered.

The useful purchase question is narrower than “Which brand is safest?” It is whether the result being advertised applies to the exact vehicle and whether it supports the comparison you intend to make. The examples below were checked on 7 November 2026. They illustrate different rating bodies’ rules, not a universal certification system.

## Read the rating as a record, not a badge

Open the assessment organization’s own result and keep its link with the quotation. Identify the program, rating or award year, assessed body style, applicable variants and any production qualification. Distinguish the tested example from the wider variants the organization explicitly covers. A photograph of a similar car, a sales brochure or a shared platform does not answer that question.

This guide recommends a two-column comparison: what the published assessment covers, and what the seller can establish about the offered unit. Ask for manufacturer-linked configuration evidence and the build label, with the VIN identifying the vehicle concerned. Treat missing information as unresolved. A successful VIN decode alone is not proof of every installed safety option.

| Question | Evidence to compare | Decision if it does not match |
|---|---|---|
| Which program and year? | Original result, award year and current status | Do not use an undated badge as the comparison |
| Which market and body? | Published applicability versus original sales specification and body style | Do not transfer coverage by model name |
| Which production period? | Rating cutoff versus actual build date and any stated VIN boundary | Obtain evidence for the correct production group |
| Which equipment? | Standard rating or named optional pack versus factory configuration | Do not claim the optional-pack result without the pack |
| Are updates a condition? | Published remedial condition versus completion evidence for that VIN | Keep eligibility unresolved until documented |
| Is this used unit intact? | Condition and repair inspection, separately from the rating | Do not present a historical result as a condition guarantee |

## Euro NCAP: equipment and time answer different questions

Euro NCAP explains that some vehicles have dual ratings: one for standard equipment across the European range and another with an optional safety pack. The higher result is not a free upgrade for every vehicle wearing the same badge. If a quotation relies on that result, identify the actual pack rather than accepting a generic list of driver-assistance features.

The test year matters because assessment requirements evolve. Euro NCAP describes validity of up to six years, with review of significant updates. Its FAQ adds an important production distinction: units built during the validity period retain their rating, while newly built units after expiration become unrated. Expiration is therefore not a claim that an older vehicle suddenly deteriorated, nor permission to attach the old result to later production.

Keep rating date, build date and first-registration date in separate fields. An old assessment may remain relevant to an earlier-built used car without being equivalent to a result under newer assessment criteria. Do not apply this Euro NCAP rule automatically to ANCAP or another program. [Euro NCAP’s explanation](https://www.euroncap.com/how-to-read-the-stars/) and [FAQ](https://www.euroncap.com/faq/) provide the distinction.

## ANCAP ATTO 3: an example where remedial evidence changes eligibility

The opened ANCAP record covers Australian front-wheel-drive BYD ATTO 3 vehicles. It specifies production from 21 November 2022, after VIN LGXCE4CBXN2131695. It also covers Australian-supplied vehicles built from May 2022 that received the specified brand-initiated updates to the centre rear and front passenger seating positions. Earlier vehicles without those updates are unrated. New Zealand-supplied vehicles have a separate rating.

For an earlier Australian unit, a supplier saying “the model has five stars” has not resolved the key question. Request evidence linking completion of the relevant updates to that vehicle. Do not reinterpret the VIN cutoff as a worldwide manufacturing rule, or infer Australian coverage for a China-market car. This is a documentary purchasing example, not instructions to alter seats, restraint anchorages or airbag controls. Use the [current ANCAP result](https://www.ancap.com.au/safety-ratings/byd/atto-3/e5634a) alongside its [original Australian announcement](https://www.ancap.com.au/media-and-gallery/media-releases/5affe0).

## IIHS: the organization decides extensions

IIHS explains that it reviews whether changes affect crash performance before carrying ratings forward. Extensions to related models are assessed case by case; battery-electric variants require separate testing. Platform sharing, or a seller’s argument that two versions are mechanically similar, does not authorize the buyer to extend a rating.

Award lists can also contain production cutoffs. In the 2025 Top Safety Pick list, the 2025–26 Hyundai Elantra four-door sedan’s Top Safety Pick+ entry applies only to vehicles built after October 2024. That wording concerns build date, not the day a dealer registered or exported the car. It is a bounded example from that award list, not a statement about every Elantra worldwide or a substitute for its detailed assessment. See [IIHS methodology](https://www.iihs.org/ratings/about-our-tests) and the [2025 award list](https://www.iihs.org/ratings/top-safety-picks/2025).

## NHTSA: a matched rating still needs a fair comparison

After establishing coverage, check whether the comparison itself is valid. NHTSA restricts frontal and overall-score comparisons to vehicles in the same class whose weights differ by no more than 250 pounds. Its side and rollover comparisons have broader applicability. A single ranking that ignores these differences can mislead even when each individual score was copied correctly.

NHTSA also explains that a safety-concern symbol can accompany a high star rating. Read the concern rather than retaining only the stars. “Not Rated” for a crash condition means that condition was not tested; it is not a low numerical score. These are NHTSA-specific interpretations, not conversion rules between its stars and another program’s award. [NHTSA ratings guidance](https://www.nhtsa.gov/ratings).

## Decide what the evidence allows you to buy

If the published coverage, production boundary and equipment match, record the rating as supported for that configuration. Keep the used vehicle’s repair condition, outstanding safety campaigns and destination registration questions separate. The assessment does not inspect the unit being sold today or issue permission to register it abroad.

If only a removable documentary gap remains, ask for that exact evidence before treating the rating as a purchase advantage. For example, a factory pack record answers a different question from proof of the ATTO 3 updates. If the market or body falls outside published coverage, remove the claimed rating from the comparison unless the assessment body confirms applicability. A lower price does not repair the missing link.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does an expired Euro NCAP result make an older used car unrated?

Not automatically. Euro NCAP distinguishes units built during its validity period from later production. Confirm the applicable record and build date; do not erase that distinction using the date of resale.

### Can I use the rating of a related vehicle with the same platform?

Only rely on coverage the assessment body establishes. IIHS describes case-by-case extensions and separate testing for battery-electric variants. A supplier’s similarity claim is insufficient.

### Does five-star coverage prove the vehicle is accident-free and registrable?

No. Coverage describes an assessment’s scope. Current condition and destination eligibility need their own evidence. This article does not establish either for any offered VIN.

### What should I ask for when the seller sends only a badge?

Request the original assessment link, exact sales-market specification, build date and configuration record. Then ask only for additional evidence the published conditions make relevant, such as an optional pack or completed manufacturer updates.
